whatis.intro: Marginal cost is what one more case costs you to buy, pick and deliver. You find it by dividing the change in total cost by the change in cases. For a distributor, that includes any truck or route the new volume adds.

cards.title: What it counts
cards.body: The costs that rise with every case you ship: product, picking labor and fuel per drop. In the calculator's example, that is $18.00 a case.
cards.alt: Plus sign, for the costs each extra case adds

cards.title: What it leaves out
cards.body: Rent, insurance and office pay you already carry at today's volume. They stay put when one more account comes on, so the next case does not pay for them.
cards.alt: Minus sign, for fixed costs today's volume already carries

cards.title: When a fixed cost steps in
cards.body: A second truck or a new route lands all at once. Spread $6,000 across the 1,200 extra cases that need it, and each case carries $5.00 more.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for a step cost spread across new cases

look.h2: What to look for before you trust the number
look.intro: The math is simple. The inputs are where it goes wrong. Check these three before you quote off the result.

steps.title: Costs in the right bucket
steps.body: A driver's wage stays fixed until you add a route. Fuel and picking labor move with every case. File one in the wrong place and the answer moves.

steps.title: Cases that are really new
steps.body: Count only volume you would not ship anyway. An account that moves its Tuesday order to Friday adds no cases.

steps.title: The same time period
steps.body: Monthly fixed costs need monthly cases. Mix in a weekly case count and the step cost per case comes out about four times too high.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits in the calculation
vos.h3: Order taking sits inside your cost per case
vos.body: VOS does not calculate your costs. It changes one input: the time your team spends taking each order. Your customers order by voice in the VOS app, and each order reaches you confirmed, in the format you already use.
